messages:
alice_support: FYI getting a high-priority escalation from ACME — multiple customers seeing p95 ~2s -> p95 ~6s and p99 spikes to 18-22s on /v1/generate. Customer says requests are queued. They provided a few request IDs.

alice_support: Repro from ACME (they say happens intermittently under sustained traffic):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"opt-m-30b","input":"<~2k tokens>","max_tokens":512}'
```

alice_support: They report 30 concurrent clients, each ~1 r/s over 5m -> queueing started ~5m in. Tenant: acme-inc-42. Customer impact: UI timeouts and retries.

sre_jordan: Thanks — tagging eng_oncall. @eng_oncall_maya can you check admission queue depth and pool backpressure for acme-inc-42? Also need trace ids if available.

eng_oncall_maya: looking now. Saw an alert for pool gpu-pool-eu-west-2 around 11:12 UTC: admission_queue_depth > 900 for ~3m. Running quick query on ingress metrics...

infra_bot: ALERT: admission_queue_depth{pool="gpu-pool-eu-west-2",tenant="acme-inc-42"} = 1124 for 2m (threshold 500).

eng_oncall_maya: KV cache hit rates look normal. Worker utilization on that pool is pinned ~98% on a subset of nodes (node-17, node-18). There's a small set of long-running requests (seq_len > 2048) holding slots.

sre_jordan: Any evidence of auth/token retries or upstream 401/403 that could cause retry storms?

alice_support: Customer's logs show a flurry of 429s then client retries with exponential backoff but some with minimal backoff. They also rotated an API key ~10m before spike — might be related.

eng_oncall_maya: Ok plausible. Two-pronged mitigation: 1) throttle per-tenant concurrent requests (lower the limit for acme-inc-42 temporarily) or 2) route their traffic to a lower-cost fallback model (opt-m-8b) to free slots. Also we can enable fast-fail for requests that exceed queue timeout to avoid head-of-line blocking.

sre_jordan: Agreed. Immediate steps I recommend:
- Temporarily reduce tenant concurrency for acme-inc-42 from 120 -> 40 via runtime config.
- Enable queue-timeout=4s fast-fail for non-critical routes.
- Graceful restart of node-17 (drain+reboot) to reclaim stuck workers.

Can someone run the concurrency change and enable fast-fail?

eng_oncall_maya: I'll apply the runtime override for tenant concurrency now and flip queue-timeout for that tenant. Pasting command I used:
```
redwoodctl runtime override set --tenant acme-inc-42 --key concurrency_limit --value 40
redwoodctl runtime override set --tenant acme-inc-42 --key queue_timeout_ms --value 4000
```

eng_oncall_maya: Done. Watching metrics.

infra_bot: NOTICE: runtime.override applied {tenant="acme-inc-42",concurrency_limit="40",queue_timeout_ms="4000"}

eng_oncall_maya: After override: admission_queue_depth dropped from 1124 -> 180 over ~40s. p95 for /v1/generate back to ~1.1s, p99 down to ~5.6s and still trending down.

alice_support: Passing update to ACME: "We applied temporary concurrency limits and queue timeouts which reduced queueing; we're monitoring and will coordinate a follow-up. If you're able, please avoid key rotations while we stabilize." :thumbsup:

customer_acme_inc: Appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll pause the key rotation and will test on our side. Please let us know when it's safe to resume.

sre_jordan: Follow-ups for later:
- Add tenant-level heuristic to auto-detect token-rotation retry storms (backoff detection).
- Tighter default queue-timeout for large-seq requests or opt-in routing to fallback models.
- Postmortem if recurrence occurs.

eng_oncall_maya: I'll schedule the node drain + healthcheck tonight during low traffic and add a short runbook for support to apply the runtime overrides.

alice_support: Thanks everyone — marking as resolved for now, will reopen if ACME reports new errors. Link to alert: https://redwood.status/alert/ACME-3955

sre_jordan: Good job. Keep an eye on similar tenants; might be a pattern. :eyes:
